observations: What I read: this request (the script for 05-1 to 05-4, boundary context and first reading), source/original.txt and the 2026-11-12 revision notes (screen sections, AI voice consent, label wording). Images I opened with Read and looked at: workflow/review/page-05.png, assets/panels/05-1.png and 05-3.png, plus page-04.png and page-06.png for the boundaries. I did not open 05-2 or 05-4 panel art separately; I judged them from the lettered page.

The text matches the source exactly. 05-1: Ananya's 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' and the PATIENT DETAILS label with all six items in the user's order. 05-2: 'May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?' and Ravi's 'Yes, I agree.', plus the AI VOICE CONSENT label. 05-3: Ravi's 'I've been feeling tired lately.' and the SOAP NOTES label. 05-4: 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' None of the labels ends with a full stop. They are consistent with each other and with page 6, so the missing full stop on the consent label is a consistent style, not an error.

05-1 label against the laptop, checked in the art. The art is 1392x736, scaled to rect [24,24,976,520] (scale about 0.70). The laptop screen is at art x10-405, y260-690, which maps to page x31-308, y206-508. The label spans about x33-325, y225-490, so it covers almost the whole drawn screen, including the six icon cards and the mic toggle drawn OFF. The decision in REVISION-2026-11-11 is that section names and contents are lettered over the text-free screen. The laptop is still clearly identified by the bezel corner above the label and the keyboard below it, and the label lists 'AI mic option', so hiding the OFF toggle does not suggest the AI is already listening. Ananya's hand on the desk (art x470-640, which maps to page x353-473) is clear of the label's right edge at x≈325. Acceptable.

05-3 tail and label, checked in the art. The art is 1024x992, scaled to the panel at (24,922), scale about 0.547; I checked it with the watch, art (905,700) maps to page (519,1305). Ravi's hand at his neck is at art x630-690, y215-290, which maps to page x369-401, y1040-1081. The tail tip at about page (387,1045) meets the edge of his fingers where hand and hair meet, below the ear. The narrow tip hides only a few pixels of outline; the neck-rubbing gesture and the face (eyes, mouth) stay fully readable, so this is acceptable. The SOAP NOTES label (x25-273, y1160-1457) covers the left card column of the laptop screen. Its right edge stops just left of the glowing mic waves (art x460, which maps to page x≈276), so the key 'AI listening' icon stays visible. Ravi's elbow (page x276-314, y1108-1179) is also clear.

05-2 balloons: the question balloon (right edge about x395) and 'Yes, I agree.' (left edge about x398) almost touch. They read correctly left to right at the same height. Their tails go in opposite directions: the question's tail goes down-left to Ananya's head (tip at her crown, about x280, y738), and Ravi's long diagonal tail ends beside his head (about x665, y745). That diagonal passes about 10 px below the bottom-left corner of the consent label, crossing neither the label nor the laptop. The tight join is a polish point, not a misreading risk. 'talk?' ends about 14 px inside its border. 05-4: the caption sits on the empty upper wall, clear of Ananya's head (top about y1135) and the back of Ravi's head (to the right of x930).

Natural scan: in 05-1 the greeting balloon is the highest element (y40-178) and is read first, then the large PATIENT DETAILS label below it at the left (from y225). In 05-2 the question, then 'Yes, I agree.', then the consent label run left to right along the same top band. In 05-3 Ravi's balloon at the top left comes before the SOAP NOTES label at the bottom left. The 05-4 caption at the top comes last.

Proximity: the only tight cluster is the pair of 05-2 balloons, which are edge to edge. They read in the correct order, and the tails send the reader to Ananya and Ravi in turn, so the consent question is not skipped or merged. The PATIENT DETAILS label at the left could draw a glance first, but it is lower than the balloon and is screen information that does not depend on the greeting order.

readingReview.comparison: The first reader's order (greeting, consent question, consent, consent label, symptom, closing caption) is the same as the script order 05-1[1,2], 05-2[1,2,3], 05-3[1,2], 05-4[1]. Concerns, each judged: (1) The PATIENT DETAILS label might be glanced at before the greeting. The balloon is clearly higher and is read first, and the label is screen information, so this is acceptable. (2) The 05-2 balloons edge to edge. The order is correct and the opposite tails separate the speakers, so this is acceptable as a polish point. (3) 'talk?' near the border. It is inside by about 14 px, so this is acceptable. (4) The PATIENT DETAILS label covers most of the laptop. This follows the user-confirmed decision to letter section content over the text-free screen, the laptop stays identifiable, and no hand or face is covered (checked in the 05-1 art), so this is acceptable. (5) The SOAP label covers the left part of the laptop. The mic icon, the key visual, stays visible, so this is acceptable. (6) No full stop on the consent label. This is consistent label style, so it is acceptable. (7) Ravi's 05-3 tail ends at his ear and hair. The tip meets the edge of his fingers and hair, but not the face, and the gesture still reads, so this is acceptable. (8) No spoken reply to 'I've been feeling tired lately.' on this page. The listening caption and Ananya's attentive face carry it, and 06-2 gives her reply, so this is acceptable. No unresolved differences.
